newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germans eating more bread as lifestyles change.
newsitem.headline: Germans eating more bread as lifestyles change.

text.p: German bread consumption is rising because of lifestyle changes encouraging eating outside the home, the grain and food research association GMF said on Thursday.
This trend was helping reverse sharp falls in bread consumption during the 1970s and Germany may even recapture levels seen in the 1950s, it said in a statement at a news conference.
GMF, an independent association advising grain producers and processors, said Germans were eating more bread-based snack meals during the day and at the main meal in the evening.
This "Anglo-Americanisation" of eating habits reflected higher female employment rates, increased spending power and leisure pursuits outside the home.
Per-capita consumption of 84.4 kilograms in 1996/97 (July/June) was up by three percent from 1995/96.

Average daily consumption in 1997 could reach 231 grams after hitting 225 grams in 1996. This figure had risen steadily in the 1990s after sinking to 190 grams in the first half of the 1970s and recovering to just over 200 grams in the 1980s.
Bread consumption in the 1950s was above 250 grams a day.
Annual grain consumption by the German milling industry has been steady for many years at around seven million tonnes, of which 85 percent is wheat and the remainder rye.
GMF said a trend towards wholemeal products developed in the 1980s was fading and light baking flour would increase its share of all flours used by bakeries from 56 percent at present.
